pageProps.body:
📚 Banned & Targeted Books|禁書登記

Related: 📕 Book Censorship under the NSL | 🐑 Sheep Village

The Hong Kong government has repeatedly refused to publish a list of banned books — in July 2026 the Secretary for Security said it never would. So there is no official catalogue of what the city has tried to make vanish. This page is an unofficial one: a growing registry of the titles that have been declared seditious, pulled from library shelves, seized in bookshop raids or stopped at customs, assembled from the court cases and news reports that actually named them. Where a cover can be shown, it is — to help readers recognise a book and look it up. For the cases themselves, see 📕 Book Censorship under the NSL.

This list is partial and ongoing. It grows as new titles are seized, and much is never named publicly — the 60-plus Taiwan books taken from the Waiting Bird / As One group in 2026, for instance, were never itemised. If you can add a title, a cover or the case it belongs to, please contribute.

The landmark: the Sheep Village trilogy

The three picture books that became the first works a Hong Kong court declared "seditious publications" — the template for everything that followed. Published by the General Union of Hong Kong Speech Therapists; five of its members were jailed for sedition in 2022. The archive preserves all three in full — read them in the Sheep Village viewer.

Seized, pulled and prosecuted

Titles named in the bookshop raids and library purges of 2023–2026. Click a cover to look the book up in a library catalogue.

Cover images are low-resolution reproductions shown for identification (fair use), self-hosted rather than hotlinked; sourced from Open Library and, for the Sheep Village trilogy, the archive's own preserved copies.

Removed from the public libraries

Separately from the shop raids, Hong Kong Public Libraries cleared its own shelves after the 2020 security law. The scale is only knowable second-hand, because the Leisure and Cultural Services Department has never published the list: Ming Pao counted at least 195 Chinese-language hard-copy titles pulled over two years and — via Al Jazeera — put it at more than 40% of "political-theme" books and videos removed since 2020; The Collective found 255 Chinese-language e-books gone over three years; and HKFP had already found 29 Tiananmen titles axed by 2021. For several authors the libraries removed their entire output. The named titles below come mostly from HKFP's itemised reporting; where an author has a page here — such as Joshua Wong, or the Hong Kong 47 defendants Benny Tai and Albert Ho — it is linked. Original Chinese titles and covers can be added over time (see #38).

TitleAuthorYearPulled
I Am Not a Hero · I Am Not a Kid (commentary collections)Joshua Wong2016First round, Jul 2020
My Journeys for Food and Justice (travel writing)Tanya Chan2014First round, Jul 2020
On the Hong Kong City-State (and five of his other titles)Chin Wan (Horace Chin)2012First round, Jul 2020
On Hong Kong NationalismHKU Student Union2014Reported banned, 2021
The Future of Constitutionalism in Hong Kong trilogy — The Future of Rule of Law · …of Democracy · …of "Two Systems, One Country" (and all his works)Benny Tai2015Second round, 2021
Beneath the Keystone – 18 Years in Politics (and all her prose and Jin Yong studies)Margaret Ng2018Third round, 2023
The Politics of Emotion (and all his titles)Hui Po-keung2018Third round, 2023
An Oral History of the Democratic Movement of Hong Kong in the 1980s (and all his work)Ma Ngok2012Third round, 2023
Prisoner of the State: The Secret Journal of Zhao ZiyangZhao Ziyang2009Tiananmen titles
Big Rivers Going to the East (memoir)Szeto Wah2011Tiananmen titles
Hong Kong, the Light Soy Sauce · China, the Old Soy Sauce (and all ten of his cartoon books)Zunzi (Wong Kei-kwan)20192023

Books by former lawmakers Raymond Wong and Albert Ho were also pulled in the 2021 round, though specific titles were not named in the reporting. Aggregate figures and the named examples are documented by HKFP (which itemised the titles above); the broader purge, the "40% of political titles" figure and the Tiananmen removals are corroborated by Al Jazeera and RFA.

How this registry is built

Because no official list exists, this one is assembled from primary reporting and court records — each title is here because a named case, raid, removal or seizure put it there, cited on the main book-censorship page. It is deliberately conservative: a book is listed only when a source names it, which is why broad seizures that were never itemised do not yet appear. Submissions — a cover scan, a title, the case it belongs to — are welcome through the archive's submission channels.

Sources

  • 📕 Book Censorship under the NSL — the cases each title is tied to, with their sources.
  • 🐑 Sheep Village — the trilogy, the trial, and the preserved books.
  • Open Library: Let Only Red Flowers Bloom (Emily Feng, Crown, 2025).
  • Yang Du's The Unburned Book (未燒書) is discussed in Lingua Sinica.
  • HKFP: 'Not recommended' reading — the books Hong Kong is purging from public libraries (26 May 2023) — the itemised source for the library removals above.
  • Al Jazeera: Tiananmen books disappear from Hong Kong library shelves (18 May 2023) — the "40% of political titles" figure (citing Ming Pao) and the Tiananmen removals.
  • RFA: Hong Kong libraries remove books for 'violating' national security law (24 Nov 2021) — the 2021 round.
Backlinks

noteIndex.title: SHKO(Save Hong Kong Online)
noteIndex.body:
[![Great Extinction](/assets/extinctions.jpeg)](/notes/wx39zljncctue32jn06u29u/) 
> (_Courtesy: [Hong Kong Freepress](https://hongkongfp.com/2021/11/28/explainer-over-50-groups-gone-in-11-months-how-hong-kongs-pro-democracy-forces-crumbled/), 2021_) 

SHKO (Save Hong Kong Online) is a community-driven project dedicated to preserving the rapidly disappearing websites and online resources of Hong Kong’s civil society and independent media since 2019. In response to the sweeping shutdowns caused by political changes in Hong Kong, we aim to safeguard digital heritage before it vanishes. This project is anonymous, open source, and supported by a global network of contributors.

While most sites in our archive were forced offline due to Hong Kong’s political deterioration, it’s important to note that [[RFA Cantonese|sites.rfa_cantonese]] is the only site here closed not because of Hong Kong’s situation, but due to internal political decisions in the United States.

Explore our full list of preserved sites and archives on the [Collections page](/notes/wx39zljncctue32jn06u29u/).

Recent work: documenting the [[Hong Kong Fire 2025|hong-kong-fire-2025]] tragedy at Wang Fuk Court (168 dead, ongoing probes into flammable mesh/foam, bid-rigging, and a judge-led review), including activism, timeline, and investigation subpages; and the [[⚖️ Jimmy Lai case|faces-of-the-crackdown.jimmy-lai]] — Apple Daily founder sentenced to 20 years under the National Security Law (Feb 2026), with coverage of press freedom impact and international response; and [[🎵 Glory to Hong Kong|glory-to-hong-kong]] — the 2019 protest anthem and the 2024 court order that made it the first song banned in Hong Kong since the 1997 handover; and [[📕 Book Censorship under the NSL|book-censorship]] — how Hong Kong criminalised the printed word, from the banned Sheep Village children's-book trilogy (whose speech-therapist authors were jailed for sedition) and purged public libraries to the 2026 bookshop raids; and [[🗽 Statues & Monuments|statues]] — how Hong Kong's public monuments to Tiananmen and the 2019 protests (the Pillar of Shame, the Goddess of Democracy, Lady Liberty) were removed, seized as police evidence, and driven into exile abroad; and [[⚖️ The Hong Kong 47|hong-kong-47]] — the largest National Security Law case, in which 45 pro-democracy figures were jailed for up to 10 years over a 2020 opposition primary election; and [[🕯️ Tiananmen Vigil|tiananmen-vigil]] — the thirty-year Victoria Park candlelight vigil for the 1989 crackdown, the largest June 4th commemoration on Chinese soil, now banned and its organisers jailed; and [[✊ Faces of the Crackdown|faces-of-the-crackdown]] — a human index to the publishers, students, unionists and clergy jailed, exiled or tried under the National Security Law; and [[🎬 Films & Documentaries|films]] — the protest movement on film, a decade of documentaries and features (Ten Years, Revolution of Our Times, the Joshua Wong doc) now largely banned or unshowable in Hong Kong, gathered with their trailers; and [[📰 Press Freedom under Siege|press-freedom]] — how one of Asia's freest presses was dismantled in five years, from the raids that closed Apple Daily and Stand News to the revived sedition law now reaching lone online reporters; and [[🗣️ Cantonese Under Pressure|cantonese]] — how Hong Kong's mother tongue, spoken by nearly everyone yet official to no one, is squeezed in schools and officialdom, from the Education Bureau's 2014 "not an official language" gaffe to a prestigious school's 2026 attempt to forbid Cantonese in a graduation video; and [[🖼️ Culture Under Control|culture-under-control]] — how Hong Kong's flagship cultural institutions, above all the M+ museum, quietly police their own programmes under the National Security Law, from Ai Weiwei's withheld Tiananmen photograph at the 2021 opening to the 2026 cancellation of a Hou Hsiao-hsien classic for unexplained "technical reasons."

## Goals
- To preserve as much information as possible before its disappearance during Hong Kong's great transition
- To illustrate a viable method that everyone can use to help preserve online heritage with no pains
- To demonstrate global collaborations to save local digital heritages with best practices

## Quick Facts

We are working on over dozens of [[websites or online causes | sites]] in Hong Kong in the past two decades which has been forced to shutdown or at the brink of disappearing. We'd welcome anyone help [[contribute | participation]] to the content and/or [[sponsor | sponsorship]] our program to sustain it together. 

Examples:
- [[sites.appledaily]] (Extincted)
- [[sites.inmediahk]] (In Danger)
